events.city.the_address_that_moved.title: The Address That Moved
events.city.the_address_that_moved.body: The number on the paper is a shutter with a padlock through it, and the shutter has been down long enough for someone to have painted over it twice. The street carries on either way. Nobody in sight looks like they are from here either.
events.city.the_address_that_moved.out.f: You walk the block twice, spot the same name over a doorway two streets across, and someone there is expecting you. Roughly.
events.city.the_address_that_moved.out.a: You walk the wrong way with real conviction for the better part of an hour, and arrive back at the same shutter from the other side.
events.city.the_address_that_moved.out.c: Standing on a corner with a map open is an advertisement, and it is read. Nothing happens, exactly. You simply become someone people have noticed.
events.city.the_address_that_moved.choic: Ask in the shop on the corner
events.city.the_address_that_moved.out.p: The woman behind the counter knows exactly where they went, why, and what she thinks about it. You get the address and most of the opinion.
events.city.the_address_that_moved.out.m: You have the word for the street and the word for the number and nothing to put between them. She is patient. It does not help.
events.city.the_address_that_moved.out.s: He is certain, and he is wrong, and you find that out at the far end of a long road.
events.city.the_address_that_moved.choic: Pay someone to walk you there
events.city.the_address_that_moved.out.s: It costs less than the hour would have and takes six minutes. You are led there without a word and left at the door.
events.city.the_outskirts.title: The Outskirts
events.city.the_outskirts.body: Warehouses, then a builder's yard, then the first traffic lights in four days. The city announces itself in reverse: the ugly edge first, the part on the postcard somewhere behind it. Whatever the road has done to you is about to be visible under proper lighting.
events.city.the_outskirts.out.through_be: You get in ahead of whatever the evening does to these roads, and it is almost anticlimactic.
events.city.the_outskirts.out.an_hour_of: Three roundabouts, two of them twice, and a sign for the centre that points at a wall.
events.city.the_outskirts.out.strip_ligh: Strip lights, a hot plate, and a queue of people who all did the same thing you did to get here. You eat properly for the first time in days.
events.city.the_outskirts.out.into_the_w: It goes into the water at the edge of a builder's yard and that is the end of it. Somebody, at some point, is going to want a conversation about that.
events.city.the_outskirts.out.the_back_r: There is a service road behind the depots that the map does not commit to. It works.
events.city.the_outskirts.out.the_long_w: The obvious way in has been closed for months, and the diversion was signposted by somebody who enjoyed it.
events.city.the_outskirts.out.waved_down: A hand goes up on the hard shoulder, and there is a long, unhurried look at your documents while the traffic goes past.
events.city.the_last_kilometre.title: The Last Kilometre
events.city.the_last_kilometre.body: The street is in the grid you have been carrying in your head for weeks and it is narrower than the version in there. Somebody is unloading crates. Somebody else is arguing on a balcony. None of it knows how far you have come, and there is no reason it should.
events.city.the_last_kilometre.out.nothi: You arrive. It takes about four minutes and nobody marks the occasion, which is broadly what arriving is.
You get there. Whatever was supposed to be waiting at the end of it does not appear to have travelled with you.
events.city.the_last_kilometre.out.clean: A shirt, a wash and twenty minutes. It buys nothing you could point at and it changes every conversation you have for a week.
events.city.the_last_kilometre.out.uprig: You walk in on your own feet, fed, clean, owing nobody, and knowing exactly what the road cost because you paid all of it yourself. Very few finish it this way.
events.city.the_last_kilometre.out.the_s: The shirt fits and the wash was worth having, and neither reaches whatever the road took out of you on the way here. You arrive presentable. That is all you arrive.
events.city.the_last_kilometre.choice.fi: Find who you were sent to
events.city.the_last_kilometre.out.they_: They were told to expect you a fortnight ago and had stopped believing it. There is food, and a bed, and a favour banked for later.
events.city.the_last_kilometre.out.a_shu: A shutter down and a name that means nothing to anybody on the street. You sit on the step for a while.
events.city.the_last_kilometre.out.recog: Somebody clocks you from across the road before you reach the door, and starts walking the other way rather fast.
